rows.description: A toddler shakes the head to say no, often before speaking clearly, showing refusal or a wish for control. It is meaningful communication that adults can respond to with respect.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler turns the head toward a caregiver to engage and away to end an interaction or feed. Respecting a turn-away shows the child that signals matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler with dropped, loose shoulders in a caregiver's arms shows safety and relaxation, and tense shoulders may show distress or pain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, trust, hurt

rows.description: A toddler hunches or raises the shoulders toward the ears when shy or with a stranger, a protective sign of unease. Letting the child warm up is respectful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, anger, shyness

rows.subtype: Raising arms to be picked up [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler raises both arms to ask to be lifted, a clear request for closeness or comfort. Responding builds security, and it is normal at this age.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler flaps or spreads the arms with excitement, at a favourite person or a running game. It shows joy and energy rather than aggression.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, hostility, excitement

rows.description: A toddler claps at a song or an achievement, sharing joy and copying others. Clapping together is a happy social routine.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler reaches and clasps hands to request or hold an object or person, showing desire and affection. It builds early bonding and communication.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Beckoning and thumbs-up copied from adults [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler copies come-here and thumbs-up gestures from adults without full understanding. Meaning follows the response the child sees.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler waves bye-bye and points to share interest, first signs of shared meaning. Pointing is a key step in language, and adults respond by naming the object.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
